title: TE Erwin Morrison v. Philadelphia Presbytery
disposition_detail: The Assembly adopted its special Judicial Commission's judgment rejecting the improper-debate specification, sustaining the constitutional challenge, annulling Presbytery's transfer instruction, and directing safeguards.
first_summary: Philadelphia Presbytery ordered Christ Church, Oreland’s Session to transfer three ruling elders while their judicial cases were on appeal. The General Assembly adopted its special Judicial Commission’s judgment rejecting the improper-debate specification for insufficient documentation but sustaining the constitutional challenge: BCO 12-5 and the separation of church-court powers reserve membership control to the Session, which correctly withheld transfer during pending judicial process. The judgment annulled Presbytery’s instruction and imposed three-year constitutional-inquiry safeguards, plus Digest purchase and officer review.

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: The 16th Assembly identified Case #4 as Morrison's complaint; the 17th Assembly adopted the special Judicial Commission's statement and judgment as its own.
evidence_notes.dispute: Presbytery instructed the Session to transfer three ruling elders while their judicial proceedings remained pending.
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: The debate specification failed for insufficient documentation; the constitutional specification succeeded because membership control belonged to the Session under BCO 12-5.
evidence_notes.qualifications: The judgment annulled the instruction and imposed temporary constitutional-inquiry safeguards and officer review.
